markets: Pre-revenue; operations centred in the US; no commercial sales yet; reported to have agreed an acquisition by Eli Lilly.
rationale: Pre-revenue therapy developer with no consumer brand to market and limited sponsorship budget; weak F1 fit.
changed: Agreed to be acquired by Eli Lilly in 2025

name: Arcutis Biotherapeutics
desc: California dermatology company selling Zoryve roflumilast cream, foam and solution for psoriasis, seborrheic dermatitis and atopic dermatitis.
markets: Sells Zoryve mainly in the US and Canada to dermatologists and patients; no verified wider expansion plans.
rationale: US dermatology drug seller with some patient advertising but a domestic focus; weak F1 fit.

name: ArriVent
desc: Pennsylvania clinical-stage cancer drug company whose lead candidate is furmonertinib, an EGFR inhibitor for lung cancer, licensed from China.
markets: Pre-revenue; operations centred in the US with a licence from a Chinese developer; no commercial sales yet.
rationale: Pre-revenue therapy developer with no consumer brand to market and limited sponsorship budget; weak F1 fit.

name: Biosplice Therapeutics
desc: San Diego biotech, formerly Samumed, developing Wnt pathway drugs led by lorecivivint, an injected treatment for knee osteoarthritis.
markets: Pre-revenue; no commercial sales yet, operations centred in the US; privately funded; no verified international expansion plans.
rationale: Pre-revenue therapy developer with no consumer brand to market and limited sponsorship budget; weak F1 fit.

name: Day One Biopharmaceuticals
desc: California biopharmaceutical company selling Ojemda, tovorafenib, approved for children with relapsed low-grade glioma, a brain tumour.
markets: Sells Ojemda in the US with licensing partners elsewhere; no verified own international sales.
rationale: Small paediatric cancer drug seller with no consumer brand; weak F1 fit.

name: NanoString Technologies
desc: Seattle life sciences tools company that sold spatial biology and gene-expression instruments such as GeoMx, CosMx and nCounter to researchers.
markets: Sold instruments to research labs in North America, Europe and Asia; now owned by Bruker after bankruptcy.
rationale: Now a Bruker unit selling research instruments to labs with no brand marketing; weak F1 fit.
changed: Filed for Chapter 11 in 2024; acquired by Bruker in 2024

name: Perfect Day
desc: California food technology company using fermentation to make animal-free whey and casein dairy proteins for food brands.
markets: Sells ingredients to US food brands; limited verified international activity; funding and operations have shrunk.
rationale: Alternative-protein ingredient maker selling mainly to food companies; sustainability story fits F1 themes but budget and scale look limited.

name: Solugen
desc: Houston chemical company making hydrogen peroxide, organic acids and plant-based chemicals through its Bioforge enzymatic and metal catalyst process.
markets: Sells chemicals to US industrial customers from its Minnesota plant; no verified international expansion plans.
rationale: B2B chemicals maker with sustainability angle and little brand marketing; modest F1 fit through technology and decarbonisation themes.

name: Xencor
desc: California biotech known for its XmAb antibody engineering platform creating bispecific antibodies for cancer and autoimmune disease.
markets: Revenue from licensing and royalties with pharma partners; operations centred in the US; no verified international expansion plans.
rationale: Pre-revenue therapy developer with no consumer brand to market and limited sponsorship budget; weak F1 fit.

name: ANI Pharmaceuticals
desc: US specialty pharmaceutical company making branded and generic drugs, led by Purified Cortrophin Gel and the blood pressure drug Inderal.
markets: Sells mainly to US pharmacies, wholesalers and hospitals; small presence in Canada; no verified expansion plans.
rationale: Domestic specialty and generic drug seller with small marketing budget and no consumer brand; weak F1 fit.

name: ArsenalBio
desc: California cell therapy company building programmable T cells for solid tumours using CRISPR gene editing and synthetic biology.
markets: Pre-revenue; no commercial sales yet, operations centred in the US; privately funded; no verified international expansion plans.
rationale: Pre-revenue therapy developer with no consumer brand to market and limited sponsorship budget; weak F1 fit.

name: Astria Therapeutics
desc: Boston clinical-stage biotech developing navenibart, a long-acting antibody injection to prevent attacks of hereditary angioedema.

name: Cardurion Pharmaceuticals

name: CG Oncology

rationale: Pre-revenue therapy developer with no consumer brand to market and limited sponsorship budget; weak F1 fit.

name: Chimerix

rationale: Now a Jazz Pharmaceuticals unit with a prescription-only cancer drug and no stand-alone marketing; weak F1 fit.

name: Cullinan Therapeutics
desc: Massachusetts biotech, formerly Cullinan Oncology, developing targeted cancer medicines including zipalertinib, an EGFR exon 20 inhibitor for lung cancer.
markets: Pre-revenue; no commercial sales yet, operations and listing centred in the US; no verified international expansion plans.

name: Gritstone bio

name: MiMedx Group

name: Neumora Therapeutics

name: Nkarta Therapeutics
desc: California cell therapy company developing off-the-shelf natural killer cell treatments for B-cell cancers and autoimmune diseases.

name: Organogenesis
desc: Massachusetts regenerative medicine company making bioactive wound care and surgical biologics, including Apligraf, Dermagraft and PuraPly.

name: Trevena

name: Aligos Therapeutics

name: Compass Therapeutics
desc: Boston clinical-stage cancer company developing antibody therapies, led by tovecimig, a bispecific antibody for biliary tract cancer.

name: Harrow Health
